steps.narration: Convert five one one base nine to base ten using powers of nine, which gives four hundred and fifteen.
Expand six r seven base eight using powers of eight, giving three hundred and ninety one plus eight r.
Set three hundred and ninety one plus eight r equal to four hundred and fifteen, then subtract to get eight r equals twenty four.
Divide twenty four by eight to find r equals three.

teach.narration: We want to find the missing digit r. Since the two numbers are in different bases, we convert both sides to base ten so we can compare them.
Start with five one one base nine. Multiply each digit by its place value, eighty one, nine, and one, to get four hundred and fifteen.
Now expand six r seven base eight. The middle digit sits in the eights place, so it is worth eight r, giving three hundred and ninety one plus eight r.
Set both base ten expressions equal, then subtract three hundred and ninety one from four hundred and fifteen to leave eight r equals twenty four.
Divide twenty four by eight to get r equals three. So the missing digit in six r seven base eight is three.

steps.narration: Subtract the actual length from the measured length to get an error of zero point zero one metres.
Divide the error zero point zero one by the actual length one point two five, and multiply by one hundred for percentage error.
Multiply zero point zero one by one hundred to get one, then divide by one point two five for zero point eight zero percent.

teach.narration: We want the percentage error in measuring the rope. First we find how far off the measurement is, then compare that error against the true length.
Subtract one point two five from one point two six. The measurement is off by zero point zero one metres.
Always divide by the actual length, not the measured one, then multiply by one hundred to turn the fraction into a percentage.
Zero point zero one times one hundred is one, and one divided by one point two five is zero point eight zero percent. That is the percentage error.

steps.narration: Rearrange the simple interest formula to make the rate R equal one hundred times interest over principal times time.
Substitute twenty four for the interest, four hundred for the principal, and three for the time in years.
Simplify two thousand four hundred over one thousand two hundred to get a rate of two percent.

teach.narration: We need the annual rate of simple interest. We start from the simple interest formula I equals P R T over one hundred.
Make R the subject of the formula, giving one hundred times I over P times T, so we isolate the unknown rate.
Put in twenty four naira for interest, four hundred naira for principal, and three years for time.
Multiply top and bottom to get two thousand four hundred over one thousand two hundred, which divides cleanly to two percent per year.

steps.narration: Multiply two over three and five over six by six to clear the denominators, giving p to q equals four to five.
Multiply three over four and one over two by four so q to r becomes whole numbers, three to two.
Scale both ratios so the shared term q reaches fifteen, giving twelve to fifteen and fifteen to ten.
Combine the two ratios at fifteen to get p to q to r equals twelve to fifteen to ten.

teach.narration: We want to join two fraction ratios into one ratio p to q to r. First we clear the fractions, then make the shared middle term q match.
Multiply both parts of two over three to five over six by six, the common denominator, which simplifies p to q to four to five.
Multiply both parts of three over four to one over two by four so q to r becomes three to two.
Now q is five in one ratio and three in the other. Their lowest common multiple is fifteen, so scale the first ratio by three and the second by five.
Since q is fifteen in both, we can join them straight across to get twelve to fifteen to ten.

steps.narration: Use the negative power rule to turn eighty one over sixteen upside down into sixteen over eighty one to the power of one over four.
Take the fourth root of sixteen and eighty one, giving two over three.
Rewrite two to the power of minus one as one over two.
Multiply two over three by one over two and cancel the twos to get one over three.

teach.title: Start · Negative indices
teach.reason: We want to evaluate this indices expression. A negative power flips a base into its reciprocal.
teach.narration: Let's evaluate eighty one over sixteen to the power of minus one quarter, times two to the power of minus one. Remember, a negative power tells us to flip the base first.

teach.title: 1) Flip for the negative power
teach.reason: Flip \frac{81}{16} upside down to \frac{16}{81} so the power becomes positive \frac{1}{4}.
teach.narration: First, flip eighty one over sixteen to sixteen over eighty one. That clears the minus sign from the power, leaving positive one quarter.

teach.title: 2) Take the fourth root
teach.reason: A power of \frac{1}{4} means the fourth root of the top and the bottom.
teach.narration: Next, a power of one quarter means the fourth root. Two to the fourth is sixteen and three to the fourth is eighty one, so the first part becomes two over three.

teach.title: 3) Change 2^{-1} to \frac{1}{2}
teach.reason: A power of −1 turns a number into its reciprocal, so 2^{-1} becomes \frac{1}{2}.
teach.narration: Now change two to the power of minus one into one over two, because any base to the power of minus one is one over that base.

teach.title: 4) Multiply the fractions
teach.reason: Cancel the common factor of 2 on top and bottom, then multiply what remains.
teach.narration: Now multiply two over three by one over two. The two on top cancels the two below, leaving one over three.

teach.title: Final answer
teach.reason: The whole indices expression simplifies to \frac{1}{3}.
teach.narration: So the value of the whole expression is one over three.

steps.narration: Break one hundred and twelve into factors of two and seven, which gives two to the fourth times seven.
Apply the product and power rules of logarithms to split log one hundred and twelve into four log two plus log seven.
Substitute the given logs and multiply four by zero point three zero one zero to get one point two zero four zero plus zero point eight four five one.
Add the two decimals carefully to get two point zero four nine one.

teach.narration: We want to find log one hundred and twelve using only log two and log seven. So we break one hundred and twelve down into twos and sevens.
Divide one hundred and twelve by seven to get sixteen, and sixteen is two to the power of four.
By the laws of logarithms, multiplication inside becomes addition outside, and the power four moves to the front of log two.
Put in the values: four times zero point three zero one zero is one point two zero four zero, plus zero point eight four five one.
Adding those two decimals gives two point zero four nine one, which is the value of log one hundred and twelve.

steps.narration: Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate, the square root of five plus the square root of three, to clear the surds below.
Expand the numerator and combine like terms to get three times the square root of fifteen plus eleven.
Use difference of two squares on the denominator to get five minus three, which equals two.
Write the simplified numerator over two to get three times the square root of fifteen plus eleven, all over two.

teach.title: Start · Rationalise the denominator
teach.reason: We want to clear the square roots from the bottom using its conjugate, \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3}.
teach.narration: Let's rationalise this surd fraction. Because the bottom has root five minus root three, we use its conjugate, root five plus root three, to clear the roots below.

teach.title: 1) Multiply by the conjugate
teach.reason: The bottom has a surd, so we multiply top and bottom by \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3} to clear it without changing the value.
teach.narration: First, multiply both the top and the bottom by root five plus root three. Doing the same to top and bottom keeps the fraction equal.

teach.title: 2) Expand the top
teach.reason: Multiply each term in the first bracket by each term in the second, then collect like terms.
teach.narration: Next, expand the top term by term. Two root fifteen plus one root fifteen gives three root fifteen, and six plus five gives eleven.

teach.title: 3) Simplify the bottom
teach.reason: Difference of two squares removes the middle surd terms on the bottom.
teach.narration: Now simplify the bottom using difference of two squares. Root five squared minus root three squared gives five minus three, which is two.

teach.title: Final fraction
teach.reason: No surd remains in the denominator, so the fraction is fully rationalised.
teach.narration: So the rationalised fraction is three root fifteen plus eleven, all over two.

steps.narration: Multiply the whole numbers twenty one and thirty four first to get seven hundred and fourteen.
Count four decimal places from both factors so the product becomes zero point zero seven one four.
Move the decimal point two places right after the seven, giving seven point one four times ten to the minus two.

teach.narration: We want the product of zero point two one and zero point three four written in standard form, with one non-zero digit before the decimal point.
Ignore the decimal points first and multiply twenty one by thirty four, which gives seven hundred and fourteen.
There are two decimal places in each number, making four in total, so we place the point to get zero point zero seven one four.
Now shift the decimal point two places right to sit after the seven. Because the original number is less than one, the power is minus two, giving seven point one four times ten to the minus two.

steps.display: n(C ∪ G) = n(C) + n(G) − n(C ∩ G)
steps.narration: Write the two-set union formula so people reading both papers are not counted twice.
Put in fifty total readers, forty Champion readers, and thirty Guardian readers.
Subtract fifty from seventy to find twenty people read both papers.

teach.narration: We want to find how many readers read both newspapers. Adding forty and thirty counts the overlap twice, so we use the two-set formula.

teach.display: n(C ∪ G) = n(C) + n(G) − n(C ∩ G)
teach.narration: The total union equals the first group plus the second group minus their intersection, which corrects for double counting.
Substitute fifty for the union, forty for Champion, and thirty for Guardian.
Forty plus thirty is seventy, which is twenty more than fifty. Those twenty extra counts are the twenty people who read both papers.

steps.narration: Move plus one across the equals sign to get P minus one equals M over five times X plus Q.
Multiply both sides by five and expand the bracket to give five P minus five equals M X plus M Q.
Subtract M X from both sides so M Q stands alone as five P minus M X minus five.
Divide by M to get Q equals five P minus M X minus five, all over M.

teach.title: Start · Make Q the subject
teach.reason: We want Q alone on one side, so we undo the outer operations around Q in reverse order.
teach.narration: Let's make Q the subject of this formula. To get Q alone, we peel off the outer operations in reverse order, starting with the plus one.

teach.title: 1) Subtract 1 from both sides
teach.reason: Take away 1 from both sides so the fraction term stands alone on the right.
teach.narration: First, subtract one from both sides. That leaves P minus one equal to M over five times X plus Q.

teach.title: 2) Multiply both sides by 5
teach.reason: Multiply every term on the left by 5 to clear the denominator 5 on the right.
teach.narration: Next, multiply both sides by five to clear the fraction. Five times P minus one gives five P minus five, equal to M times X plus Q.

teach.title: 3) Expand the bracket
teach.reason: Multiply M into both X and Q so we can separate the Q term.
teach.narration: Now expand the bracket by multiplying M into X and Q, giving M X plus M Q.

teach.title: 4) Isolate MQ
teach.reason: Subtract MX from both sides so the term with Q stands by itself.
teach.narration: Subtract M X from both sides so M Q stands alone, equal to five P minus M X minus five.

teach.title: 5) Divide both sides by M
teach.reason: Divide the entire right side by M to undo multiplying Q by M.
teach.narration: Now divide both sides by M so the M in front of Q cancels out.

teach.title: Final formula
teach.reason: Q now stands alone as the subject of the formula.
teach.narration: So making Q the subject gives Q equals five P minus M X minus five, all over M.

steps.narration: Rewrite twenty seven x cubed minus eight y cubed as three x all cubed minus two y all cubed.
Use the difference of two cubes identity, where the first bracket keeps the minus sign.
Put a equals three x and b equals two y into the rule to find the other factor is three x minus two y.

teach.narration: We are given one factor of twenty seven x cubed minus eight y cubed and need the other factor. Notice both terms are perfect cubes.
Write twenty seven x cubed as three x all cubed, and eight y cubed as two y all cubed, so we can apply the difference of two cubes.
In the difference of cubes formula, the short bracket keeps the minus sign while the long bracket has all plus signs.
With a equals three x and b equals two y, the long bracket matches the given factor, so the missing factor is three x minus two y.

steps.narration: Factorise x squared minus y squared as x minus y times x plus y equals eight.
Replace x minus y with two and divide eight by two to get x plus y equals four.
Add the two linear equations to eliminate y, leaving two x equals six.
Divide to get x equals three, then substitute back to find y equals one, giving the pair three, one.

teach.narration: We need to find x and y from these two equations. Factorising x squared minus y squared turns the harder equation into a simple straight-line one.
By the difference of two squares, x squared minus y squared splits into x minus y times x plus y.
Since x minus y is two, divide eight by two to get x plus y equals four.
Add x minus y equals two and x plus y equals four together. The y terms cancel, leaving two x equals six, so x is three.
Put x equals three into x minus y equals two to find y equals one. So the solution pair is three, one.

steps.narration: Write direct variation with the square root of x as y equals k times the square root of x.
Substitute y equals three and x equals sixteen to get four k equals three, so k equals three over four.
Put x equals sixty four into the formula: three over four times eight gives y equals six.

teach.narration: We want to calculate y when x is sixty four. Notice y varies with the square root of x, not x itself, so we first find the constant k.
Turn the variation statement into an equation by introducing a constant k: y equals k times the square root of x.
When x is sixteen, its square root is four, and y is three. Dividing three by four gives k equals three over four.
Now substitute x equals sixty four. The square root of sixty four is eight, and three over four times eight equals six.

steps.narration: Multiply every term by twelve, the common denominator, to remove all fractions.
Simplify each term to get six x plus three is greater than four x plus six.
Subtract four x and three from both sides to leave two x is greater than three.
Divide by positive two, keeping the sign unchanged, to get x is greater than three over two.

teach.narration: We want the range of x that satisfies this inequality. Clearing the fractions first makes the algebra much cleaner.
Multiply every term by twelve, the lowest common multiple of two, three, and four, giving six x plus three is greater than four x plus six.
Group x terms on the left and numbers on the right: six x minus four x is two x, and six minus three is three.
Divide both sides by positive two. Because we divide by a positive number, the greater-than sign stays the same, giving x is greater than three over two.

steps.narration: Read the first term a equals zero point five, and divide the second term by the first to get the common ratio r equals zero point one.
Use the sum to infinity formula, a over one minus r, since the ratio is smaller than one.
Substitute zero point five and zero point one to get zero point five over zero point nine, which simplifies to five over nine.

teach.narration: We want the sum to infinity of this geometric series. Since each term shrinks by a tenth, the endless sum settles to one exact fraction.
The first term a is zero point five. Dividing zero point zero five by zero point five gives the common ratio r equals zero point one.
Because the size of r is less than one, we use the sum to infinity formula, S infinity equals a over one minus r.
Substitute zero point five and zero point one to get zero point five over zero point nine. Multiply top and bottom by ten to get five over nine.
